reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 35. Nay or No: 5. Not Voting: 0. Of 40 Yea or Nay votes where the Republican majority could be computed, 40 (100%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 210 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

sponsored.note: Up to five recent sponsored bills from Congress.gov, latest introduced date first. This is not a full list of sponsored legislation.

lobbying_summary.line: Lobbying filings mention 3 of the 5 listed bills checked.
lobbying_summary.caption: From Senate lobbying disclosures (LD-2). A filing mentions this bill; it does not show what was asked for, which side the client took, or any contact with this member. Reported amounts cover the whole filing, not this bill alone.

lobbying_caption: From Senate lobbying disclosures (LD-2). A filing mentions this bill; it does not show what was asked for, which side the client took, or any contact with this member. Reported amounts cover the whole filing, not this bill alone.

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.
donor_industry.cycle_rule: House filings use the 2026 two-year cycle.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: House roll calls 1–323 of 2026 (323 votes, January 6, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the House Clerk.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.
stands_for.factual_flag: Not yet summarized: this line is built only from the official vote question and the bill's official title.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Agree — Calling on elected officials and civil society leaders to counter antisemitism and educate the public on the contributions of the Jewish-American community (H RES 1251)
votes.bill_title: Calling on elected officials and civil society leaders to counter antisemitism and educate the public on the contributions of the Jewish-American community.
votes.plain_language: This resolution calls on elected officials, faith leaders, and civil society leaders to condemn and counter acts of anti-Semitism. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports agreeing to it; a Nay opposes it.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

It was good meeting with @ShelbyTNSheriff Anthony Buckner and Chief Deputy Chuck Mays. 

I appreciate their service, leadership, and commitment to keeping our communities safe. https://t.co/tmAMNwct1Z

🏡Two places in Tennessee’s 8th Congressional District have earned spots on @livability’s list of the Top 50 Best Small Cities in America:

🏆 Germantown ranked 24th
🏆 Collierville ranked 30th

I’m proud of the work being done to make West Tennessee a great place to live, work, and raise a family!

I joined @SpeakerJohnson on the steps of the U.S. Capitol to honor the brave men and women who have served our nation in uniform. 🇺🇸

Everyday, we are grateful for our veterans’ courage, sacrifice, and commitment to defending our freedoms. https://t.co/Nla84lxw6O

On Veterans Day, we honor the brave men and women who have served our great nation. 🇺🇸

We remain grateful for their courage, service, and sacrifice. Thank you to all who have worn the uniform. https://t.co/CyTHItr0xQ

Congratulations to @Jim_Jordan on becoming the next Republican Conference Leader for the 120th Congress. 🇺🇸

I wish him well as he takes on this important role and leads our conference forward.

Today, we honor 251 years of the United States Marine Corps and the generations of Marines who have defended our nation with courage! 🇺🇸

To every Marine, thank you for your service and dedication to our country. Semper Fidelis. https://t.co/wd4HUQtItN

I was proud to secure $9,500,000 in the FY 2026 appropriations package for the West Tennessee River Basin Authority's riverbank stabilization project! 🇺🇸

This investment will help prevent erosion and protect farmland and property along West Tennessee's waterways. https://t.co/mN0PP73Az3

I was glad to secure $938,000 for campus security improvements at @utmartin in the FY2026 Appropriations package! 🇺🇸

This investment will help upgrade security measures to better protect the university's campus community in Weakley County. https://t.co/yujeLrTvEj

The FY 2026 appropriations package passed by @HouseGOP included $5,000,000 I secured for the I-69 Troy Bypass North and South project! 🇺🇸

This funding will help improve traffic flow and make travel safer and more efficient for travelers. https://t.co/Ag8nWXJ6Lr

🇺🇸 This morning I joined federal, state, and local law enforcement leaders to discuss the Memphis Safe Task Force. Together, they’ve made over 14,000 arrest including 1,500 gang members.

Thank you to @SenatorHagerty, @USAttyDunavant, United States Marshal Tyreece Miller of the https://t.co/bprxNfnqrz

🇺🇸 This morning I joined federal, state, and local law enforcement leaders to discuss the Memphis Safe Task Force. Together, they’ve made over 14,000 arrest including 1,500 gang members.

Thank you to @SenatorHagerty, @USAttyDunavant, United States Marshal Tyreece Miller of the Western District of Tennessee, and Tennessee House Speaker @CSexton25 for their leadership and commitment to making Memphis a safer place for families and businesses.

As part of the FY 2026 appropriations package, I secured $1,250,000 for campus security upgrades at @UMLambuth! 🇺🇸

This funding will be used for improving campus safety, accessibility, and the quality of the learning environment. https://t.co/l6kZiJFdYf

Last night, I joined Speaker of the Tennessee State House @CSexton25 on the field for the coin toss at the Covington High School Chargers football game!

Thank you to @CPDTN Police Chief Donna Turner, Superintendent Dr. Rebekah Byrd, Principal Carlin McGlown, Athletic Director https://t.co/GaEJdF2b5u

Earlier this Congress, I was pleased to secure $750,000 for the City of Henderson's Water Main Replacement Project in the FY 2026 appropriations package passed by @HouseGOP! 🇺🇸

This funding will help replace aging water infrastructure and provide more reliable service for https://t.co/JGdg0niSIG

Thank you, @BrendanCarrFCC, for your leadership in combating contraband cell phones in prisons. 📵

Earlier this Congress, I introduced the Cell Phone Jamming Reform Act alongside @SenTomCotton, which would support this effort to advance the deployment of cell phone jamming technology in state and federal prisons.

🚨✈️ I was pleased to secure $4,000,000 for @FlyMemphis in the FY 2026 appropriations package earlier this year!

These funds will be used to support their Memphis Terminal Modernization and Seismic Program. https://t.co/ZP6hdihC1X

🚨💧 I was proud to secure $750,000 for @JaxEnergy in the FY 2026 appropriations package passed by @HouseGOP earlier this Congress! 🇺🇸

This funding will help expand  water and wastewater infrastructure to meet the needs of Jackson’s growing community in Madison County. https://t.co/Q2jERxCghr

I had a great time attending the Milan High School vs. Nashville Collegiate Prep football game, where I had the opportunity to participate in the coin toss. 🏈

Thank you to Milan Special School District Director Dr. Versie Hamlett for the invitation, and to Milan Police Chief Bobby Sellers, Principal Jennifer Yates, and Milan Fire Chief Johnny Lock for joining me at the game. Go Bulldogs!

It was great visiting the Pope Family Farm in Gibson County. 🌾🚜

I was proud to present Justin Pope and his family with an American flag flown over the U.S. Capitol in recognition of their Century Farm, alongside the 5th, 6th and 7th generations of the Pope family. https://t.co/DXN1sslwd3

🚨🚂 I am proud to have helped secure $20.3 million in Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements grant funding for the West Tennessee Railroad!

This funding will improve over 180 miles of railroad track across West Tennessee, strengthen freight infrastructure, and support local farmers, manufacturers, and businesses. The upgrades will benefit Obion, Weakley, Gibson, Madison, Chester, and McNairy Counties.

It was good meeting with Henderson County Sheriff Brad Atkinson today.

Thank you for your leadership and dedication to keeping our communities safe. https://t.co/I4XsktZodc

Today, I attended the investiture of Dr. Keith Harris, the 17th president of Freed-Hardeman University, alongside State Representative Kirk Haston and Henderson Mayor Terry F. Bell.

Congratulations to Dr. Harris on this important milestone! https://t.co/n8088AzshE

Yesterday, I toured the St. Francis Hospital-Bartlett in Shelby County. 

Thank you to CEO Scott Smith and COO Chris Jenkins for the tour and for your work providing quality health care to the community. https://t.co/uPxU3Sz7mL

I toured the Arlington Wastewater Plant in Shelby County and met with Mayor Mike Wissman, Town Administrator Cathy Durant, and Ardurra Engineer Scott Daniels.

I am proud to have secured $1 million in federal funding for the plant’s expansion project. This funding will help https://t.co/V0o4G852hL

Roberta and I are deeply saddened about the passing of Bill Watkins. Bill co-founded one of the premier regional CPA firms, Watkins Uiberall, guiding individuals and businesses throughout the Mid-South. Bill was also involved and led a number of civic and philanthropic endeavors, https://t.co/FHll44utw8

Today, I toured the Baptist Memorial Hospital Somerville site alongside Fayette County Mayor Skip Taylor. 

Thank you to Baptist Memorial Hospital CEO and Administrator Sam Lynd, Vice President of Government and Community Relations Dr. Keith Norman, System Director of Development https://t.co/UsQz3XBjmv

This morning, I attended the 46th Annual Bartlett Fire Department Pancake Breakfast in Shelby County.

I am grateful to Chief Tommy Gately and Mayor David Parsons for hosting a great event. Thank you to our firefighters for all you do to keep our community safe. https://t.co/FsIq10Pk3o

I was honored to participate in yesterday’s roundtable marking the one-year anniversary of the Memphis Safe Task Force.
 
Thank you to all the law enforcement leaders who participated in today’s event.
 
I also appreciate @MarshaBlackburn, @AGToddBlanche, United States Attorney for the Western District of Tennessee Michael Dunavant, and @USMarshalsHQ Director Gadyaces Serralta for bringing everyone together to discuss the task force’s progress.

Tomorrow, I will be joining @MarshaBlackburn and @AGToddBlanche to discuss the great work of the Memphis Safe Task Force.

We appreciate all of the dedicated men and women in law enforcement who are making Memphis and Shelby County safer.

We are also thankful for the leadership of @GovBillLee, @MarshaBlackburn, and @SenatorHagerty in this successful endeavor.

Thank you @NewsTalk989 and @NationofJake for having me on.

Today, I had lunch with law enforcement leaders from across Gibson County at Milan’s new law enforcement training facility.

Thank you to Milan Mayor B.W. Beasley and Police Chief Bobby Sellers for hosting us. It was good to visit with Gibson County Sheriff Rodney Wright and all of the other law enforcement leadership.

I joined Tipton County Sheriff Shannon Beasley and his K-9 units for a demonstration of their work in law enforcement.

The K-9 teams demonstrated how they detect illegal drugs and assist officers in apprehending suspects. 

Thank you to Sheriff Beasley and his team for the demonstration and for their continued service to Tipton County.

Today, I joined the 25th Drug Task Force for a ride-along on I-40 to learn more about their criminal interdiction efforts.

Through specialized training and equipment, the task force works to remove illegal drugs, weapons, and criminals from our highways.

Thank you to Fayette County Sheriff Bobby Riles and Director of the 25th Judicial District Drug Task Force Bubba Thompson for providing insight into your work to keep our communities safe.

Today, I toured the Jackson Police Department’s Aviation Unit at the Jackson Regional Airport in Madison County. During the visit, I learned more about how the unit supports federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies.

Thank you to Chief Tom Corley, Sgt. Clint Patton, and Officer Joshua Michaels for the tour and for your service.

🇺🇸✈️ It was an honor to join @POTUS aboard Air Force One alongside my colleagues from Tennessee.

I’m proud to serve my constituents in West Tennessee. https://t.co/TRMmM8amHA

I met with @AlphaOmegaVet Services Board Chairman John Gurney and Executive Director Al Edward in Shelby County to discuss their work providing housing and supportive services to veterans in need. 

Thank you to the entire Alpha Omega team for your dedication to serving those who have served our country.

I had a great time attending the groundbreaking for @uthsc’s new College of Medicine Interdisciplinary Building alongside Tennessee @ltgovmcnally and Tennessee House Speaker @CSexton25.

Thank you to @UT_President Randy Boyd and Chancellor Dr. Peter Buckley for your leadership and dedication to making this project possible.

During the @WaysandMeansGOP field hearing, I heard from Orgill President and CEO Boyden Moore about how the One Big Beautiful Bill is helping his business.

Businesses can now deduct the full cost of eligible equipment upfront. This helps companies like Orgill invest in new equipment and expand operations.

I enjoyed catching up with Tennessee Safari Park Co-owner and Park Manager Claude Conley in Crockett County. 

Thank you for your dedication to animal care and for making the TN Safari Park a top tourism destination for visitors to West Tennessee. https://t.co/JNNKzt3IiB

🇺🇸 The @WaysandMeansGOP hearing in West Tennessee demonstrates how the One Big Beautiful Bill is making big, positive advances for small businesses and workers across the country.
 
We need a tax code that gives Americans certainty and permanency to plan for the future and to succeed.

🚨🇺🇸 @POTUS just signed my bill, the Improving Social Security’s Service to Victims of Identity Theft Act, into law!

Americans recovering from identity theft deserve reliable and consistent support, not layers of federal red tape.

I am proud to deliver this commonsense reform for identity theft victims across the country.

Yesterday, I joined @ToddStarnes on @Mighty990KWAM to talk about today’s @WaysandMeansGOP field hearing in West Tennessee.

The One Big Beautiful Bill gives businesses the tax relief and tools they need to hire, innovate, and succeed! 🇺🇸 https://t.co/kSZAhuxkwv

Today, the @WaysandMeansGOP Committee held a field hearing in Collierville, Tennessee.
 
This hearing gave us the opportunity to hear directly from witnesses about the pro-growth and pro-employee benefits of One Big Beautiful Bill. 
 
I am grateful to @RepJasonSmith and Orgill for helping bring the Committee to West Tennessee.

This morning I joined @iamditch on @NewsTalk989 to talk about today’s @WaysandMeansGOP field hearing in Collierville.

We discussed the importance of bringing the Committee to West Tennessee to hear directly from witnesses about how the One Big Beautiful Bill impacts their ability to succeed and compete.

I had a good time at the Bartlett Barbecue Festival yesterday in Shelby County. 🐖
 
Thank you to Bartlett Mayor David Parsons and your team for all your hard work planning this great community event. Thank you also to @BartlettTNFire Chief Tommy Gately and @BartlettPolice Chief Jeff Cox for your service and leadership.
 
Good luck to all the contestants in this year’s BBQ Festival!

I met with members of the National Hardwood Lumber Association (NHLA) today in Shelby County. 

Thank you to Executive Director Dallin Brooks, Chief Development Officer John Hester, and CEO of Classic American Hardwoods Bill Courtney for taking the time to meet with me and discuss the hardwood lumber industry.

It was good meeting with @TNHighwayPatrol’s Memphis District Captain Joe Terry in Shelby County.

I am grateful for your leadership and the team at THP who are committed to protecting our communities every day. https://t.co/u7fmcSQFPf

Yesterday I had the chance to sit down with Amelia Carlson with @WBBJ7Alerts to highlight some of my legislative wins and priorities.

From protecting victims of identity theft to fighting contraband cellphones in prisons and expanding access to early Alzheimer’s detection, I am proud to work in Congress to help West Tennesseans. https://t.co/7S9y1FUBzE

I enjoyed meeting with Haywood County Sheriff Terry Smith and Chief Deputy Jamie Moore.

Thank you both for your leadership and commitment to keeping the people of Haywood County safe. https://t.co/pquv1PibV7

I met with the Jackson Center for Independent Living (JCIL) in Madison County to hear more about their work to promote independence for people with disabilities across West Tennessee. 

Thank you to Executive Director Edward Mitchell and the JCIL team for their dedication to the people they serve.

Last night, I had the opportunity to meet with @USDOT Secretary @SecDuffy at the @FedEx World Hub in Shelby County.

The Frederick W. Smith International Airport is a logistics hub for businesses across the globe, with millions of packages moving through Memphis every day. FedEx's operation is a testament to the role Memphis plays in serving businesses and consumers worldwide.

I am glad Secretary Duffy was able to visit Memphis and the FedEx World Hub.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
